title: Quanta of Space: A Manifesto
description:
To see a World in a Grain of Sand / And a Heaven in a Wild Flower, / Hold Infinity in the palm of your hand / And Eternity in an hour. (William Blake, Auguries of Innocence)

Version 2.0: the book is now in two volumes. This volume, Volume I, keeps the manifesto: the Introduction, the six chapters with their entries, and the Kaleidohedra findings and the data set told as entries. The catalogue of all the atoms, the data work by work and the known and rediscovered shapes move to Volume II, Quanta of Space II: The DICTOnary of Atoms; every data reference reads “Volume II, A.n”. Also new in this version: the golden cuts of the Platonic solids, told in short in three places: #88 Every Platonic Solid Has Exactly Two Golden Cuts (Atoms), the golden members of Andreini's space fillings from #89, with DICTO's filling by cut cubes and octahedra (Bonds), and #89 All Five Golden Pairs Are Slices of Four-Dimensional Solids (Four dimensions). The catalogue of all the atoms, now in Volume II, adds the eight new Golden Cut solids of #88 (the DICTO-Kepler golden truncations), the four golden rhombic solids and the two Golden Cut Snub Dodecahedra (left and right hands) of #89, numbered D119 to D132, and, from DICTO Solids version 7, Cube Pearl, Golden Clasp, Hamlet and Ophelia (D106 to D109) and Kagemusha under DICTO's name, with the HexOct tiles of #75 and #86 (D110 to D118) and the DICTO Vacuus forms of #87; the two Golden Cut Icosidodecahedra (Zefiro 2011, found by DICTO independently) join the known and rediscovered shapes; Icosaxes, Unborn Axes and White Knight carry their new families, the DICTO-Kepler golden truncations and the DICTO-GTT-Solids.

Version 1.4: three new works told in short, #76 Between the Queens, #77 Face to Face and #78 The Truncated Icosahedron Star (TI Star); four new atoms in the catalogue, D102 Fallen Humpty, D103 Golden TI Star, D104 Star Halo and D105 TI Star core (105 numbered shapes); HexOct under its new title, HexOct: The Hexagonality Law; chapter references to Alicia in Wonderland version 2 and The Golden Cycle version 2.

Version 1.3: a new black cover in the style of the other books, the DICTO square with the title below in LED letters; the chapter on Aristotle's pyramids in the wording of the Collected Works; DICTO's ideas credited as proposed, specified or conjectured throughout. Version 1.2: the catalogue of all the atoms shows a picture for every shape that has one (model drawings, or the figure of its entry), pictures first and the few without at the end; the known and rediscovered shapes are listed at the end of the book; more space round titles. Version 1.1 corrected the name in About the author.

DICTO's manifesto and the overview of his geometric works: is space smooth, or built from exact pieces that fit with no gaps? From the atoms of Democritus and Plato's kit of solids to the quanta of modern physics, the book follows that question through 73 works, 71 papers in six chapters: Atoms, Bonds, Shells, Cycles, Stacking and Four dimensions, with the Kaleidohedra findings and the data set.

Its centre is the Rule of Halves: however equal balls are stacked in close-packed layers, the space between them is shared out into pieces of only finitely many kinds, every one borrowed whole or in half from the two pure stackings, a finite catalogue of quanta for every close packing, which closes into two tiles, HexOct. The catalogue of all the atoms, DICTO's 132 new shapes and his 37 new clusters, structures and networks, with the known and rediscovered shapes the work builds with and the data work by work, is Volume II, Quanta of Space II: The DICTOnary of Atoms.

The works from #52 on are told in short; the books HexOct: The Laws of Stacking, The Golden Cycle and Alicia in Wonderland: The Red & White Queens hold them in full. For my father, Alan Baker. DICTO is the artist name of (Alan) J. Baker. The cover is the DICTO square: the five Platonic solids of DICTO's name, D I C T O, in a five by five square, with the title below.

The papers, apps and data of this work are free to use; every one is open access, under the licence CC BY-SA 4.0. Computation, checking and drafting with Claude (Anthropic). More at dictospheres.com.
